studies.title: Basophil and eosinophil dynamics as predictors of omalizumab resistance in chronic spontaneous urticaria.
studies.authors: Oraloğlu, Göktürk, Süne, Ceren, Duman, Nilay, Demirel, Boratay Erin et al.
studies.abstract: Chronic spontaneous urticaria is a mast cell-driven skin disorder in which basophils and eosinophils contribute to inflammation. Omalizumab is effective for many patients, yet a subset remains resistant. Hematologic markers such as eosinophil and basophil counts have been proposed as predictors, but their utility is unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether baseline levels and post-treatment changes in eosinophil and basophil counts can serve as predictors of omalizumab resistance in patients with chronic spontaneous urticaria. This retrospective study included forty adults with antihistamine-resistant chronic spontaneous urticaria treated with monthly omalizumab. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data, including total immunoglobulin E and anti-thyroid peroxidase levels, were recorded. Absolute eosinophil and basophil counts were measured at baseline and after six months. Responders were defined as patients with a urticaria activity score ≤6 at month six. Thirty-four patients (85%) responded to omalizumab, while six (15%) were resistant. Baseline eosinophil and basophil counts tended to be lower in resistant patients, but differences were not significant. In non-responders, eosinophil and basophil counts increased significantly from baseline to month six (p = 0.002 and p = 0.007), whereas no significant changes occurred in responders. Increases in eosinophil and basophil counts during omalizumab therapy occurred mainly in non-responders, suggesting these changes may be associated with persistent disease activity rather than a direct treatment effect. However, given the limited number of non-responders in our cohort, these findings should be considered preliminary and require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

studies.title: More common than we thought: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, comorbidity burden, and long COVID risk in a national cohort.
studies.authors: Pearson, Megan L, Laraway, Bryan J, Elias, Ellen R, Bilousova, Ganna et al.
studies.abstract: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (hEDS) is a complex, underdiagnosed connective tissue disorder characterized by widespread symptoms affecting multiple organ systems. Recent clinical observations suggest that individuals with hEDS may be at increased risk for persistent symptoms following COVID-19, commonly referred to as Long COVID. Using data from over 19 million patients across the United States, we examined associations between hEDS, COVID-19 infection, Long COVID, and related chronic conditions. We identified just over 25,000 individuals with hEDS and estimated a prevalence of approximately 1 in 800, which is higher than previously recognized. Despite similar rates of COVID-19 infection between patients with hEDS and matched controls, patients with hEDS were nearly three times more likely to develop Long COVID. This risk was concentrated among patients with hEDS who also had overlapping conditions commonly seen in post-viral syndromes, including autonomic dysfunction (POTS), immune dysregulation (MCAS), and chronic fatigue (ME/CFS). Patients with hEDS also exhibited higher odds of having additional risk factors for severe or prolonged illness, including chronic lung and autoimmune conditions, depression, and cerebrovascular disease. A subgroup of patients received their hEDS diagnosis only after a COVID-19 or Long COVID diagnosis, and this subgroup was highly enriched for multimorbidity, particularly POTS and MCAS. These findings establish hEDS as more prevalent than previously recognized and identify a substantially elevated, comorbidity-driven risk of Long COVID in this population. Improved screening, earlier diagnosis, and integrated care pathways are urgently needed to support this complex and underserved patient group.

studies.title: Licoflavone B mitigates allergic rhinitis by restraining epithelial PI3K-AKT/NF-κB NLRP3 inflammasome signaling.
studies.authors: Shen, Qi, Ma, Xiaoyao, Liu, Hui, Li, Xuemin et al.
studies.abstract: Allergic rhinitis remains highly prevalent and is often incompletely controlled by current therapies, while accumulating evidence implicates epithelial PI3K-AKT/NF-κB-mediated activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in upper-airway inflammation. This study investigated whether the licorice-derived flavonoid Licoflavone B (LFB) alleviates allergic rhinitis by modulating this signaling axis. In an ovalbumin-induced murine model, allergic rhinitis-like symptoms and nasal histopathological changes were evaluated, cytokine levels were quantified by ELISA, and the activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome and PI3K-AKT/NF-κB signaling was assessed by immunoblotting. Unbiased RNA sequencing followed by KEGG and GO enrichment analyses was performed to identify potential upstream pathways. The involvement of PI3K-AKT/NF-κB signaling was further explored through PI3K-AKT reactivation with IGF-1 and TLR3 stimulation with poly(I) in vivo and in primary human nasal epithelial cells (HNEpCs). Molecular docking was also conducted to explore the potential interaction between LFB and PI3K. LFB reduced sneezing and nasal scratching, partially ameliorated epithelial thickening and inflammatory-cell infiltration, and decreased mast-cell staining. LFB also reduced the levels of IL-1β, IL-6, IL-5, IL-13, and TNF-α, as well as the expression of NLRP3-inflammasome components. RNA-sequencing analysis identified PI3K-AKT signaling as one of the major enriched pathways, and immunoblotting confirmed that LFB decreased the phosphorylation of PI3K, AKT, and p65 without substantially altering their total protein levels. In HNEpCs, IGF-1 restored pathway phosphorylation and partially reinstated cytokine and inflammasome protein expression, thereby attenuating the effects of LFB. Similarly, IGF-1 or poly(I) partially diminished the symptomatic and histological improvements induced by LFB in vivo. Molecular docking positioned LFB within the PI3K catalytic pocket, providing structural plausibility for a potential LFB-PI3K interaction. Collectively, these findings indicate that LFB alleviates ovalbumin-induced allergic rhinitis-like inflammation and is associated with reduced activation of the PI3K-AKT/NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling axis in nasal tissues, HNEpCs, and stimulated mast-cell models. The partial reversal of these effects by IGF-1 or poly(I) further supports the involvement of this signaling pathway.

studies.title: Hesperidin alleviates allergic rhinitis by inhibiting NF-κB activation and restoring nasal epithelial barrier function.
studies.authors: Zhou, Kai, Wu, Qian, Han, Jiajia, Muratov, Muzaffar et al.
studies.abstract: This study evaluated the therapeutic effect of hesperidin (HES) on allergic rhinitis (AR) in a mouse model induced by ovalbumin (OVA). After inducing AR in BALB/c mice through OVA, the severity of allergic reactions was assessed through behavioral scoring. The levels of OVA-specific IgE, histamine, and IL-6 were measured by ELISA. Pathological changes, mast cell infiltration, and protein expression, were detected using ELISA, histopathological staining, immunohistochemistry (IHC), and Western blot. The human nasal epithelial cells (RPMI-2650) were used and the epithelial barrier function was evaluated through transepithelial resistance (TEER) and FITC-dextran permeability assays. The results indicated that after HES intervention, the frequency of nasal rubbing and sneezing in mice significantly decreased, and the levels of serum OVA-specific IgE, histamine, and IL-6 also significantly reduced. Additionally, HES could alleviate nasal mucosal epithelial damage and inflammatory cell infiltration, while reducing mast cell aggregation. HES also inhibited the expression of p-p65 and p-IκBα, while enhancing the protein expression of ZO-1 and Occludin. In vitro experiments showed that HES could reverse the decrease in TEER, increase in FITC-dextran permeability, and decrease in ZO-1 and Occludin expression induced by OVA in HNEpC cells. However, when the NF-κB pathway was activated by TNF-α, the protective effect of HES was significantly diminished. In conclusion, HES could alleviate OVA-induced AR symptoms in mice by inhibiting the activation of the NF-κB signaling pathway, reducing inflammatory responses, and restoring the expression of tight junction proteins in the nasal epithelium.

studies.title: Plant-derived Alkaloids for Allergic Rhinitis: Evidence, Exposure, Safety and Translational Readiness.
studies.authors: Yang, Yaodong, Ma, Xuemei, Liu, Yuxin, Ma, Long et al.
studies.abstract: Allergic Rhinitis (AR) is an allergen-driven, IgE-mediated inflammatory disease of the nasal mucosa. Established therapies are effective for many patients, but incomplete symptom control, suboptimal adherence, and treatment preference sustain interest in new locally acting agents. Plant-derived alkaloids are frequently proposed as anti-allergic candidates; however, the literature often conflates natural compounds with semisynthetic derivatives and synthetic analogues and gives similar weight to computational predictions, cell assays, animal models, and clinical findings. A structured critical review of chemically defined alkaloids investigated in AR was conducted. Translational evidence was graded from Tier I (controlled human AR evidence) to Tier IV (cellular, omics or computational evidence), while mechanistic confidence was assessed separately. Nine canonical plant alkaloids had Tier II evidence from direct AR or combined allergic rhinitis and asthma syndrome models with nasal outcomes: berberine, corynoline, piperine, sinomenine, higenamine, dictamnine, ellipticine, warifteine and methylwarifteine. Reported effects included fewer nasal symptoms, reduced mast-cell activation, lower IgE and type 2 cytokine responses, and less eosinophilic inflammation. Warifteine and methylwarifteine constitute the most internally coherent preclinical series; most other candidates depend on a single short-duration, ovalbuminbased study. Randomisation, blinded outcome assessment, clinically relevant comparators, nasal pharmacokinetics and direct target-engagement experiments were uncommon. Safety is compound-specific and materially changes translational rank. Relevant concerns include drug-drug interactions, non-IgE-mediated mast cell activation, systemic adrenergic effects, reactive metabolites, and genotoxicity. Intranasal ipratropium provides controlled human evidence for watery rhinorrhoea, but it is a purpose-designed synthetic atropine derivative and cannot validate plant alkaloids as a therapeutic class. The available evidence therefore supports the use of selected alkaloids as lead scaffolds and mechanistic probes, but not as established AR treatments. Progress requires authenticated chemistry, parent- and metabolite-aware nasal exposure, causal studies in human nasal systems, active-comparator efficacy and safety margins appropriate for long-term treatment of a usually non-life-threatening disease.

studies.title: Development and evaluation of a microneedle-assisted transdermal delivery system for compound betamethasone in atopic dermatitis.
studies.authors: Wang, Si-Ning, Qiao, Xiaojing, Du, Fangzhi, Chen, Jing et al.
studies.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by skin barrier dysfunctio​n and immune dysregulation, which may influence topical drug penetration and therapeutic efficacy. This study evaluated a microneedle-assisted approach to enhance the cutaneous delivery of compound betamethasone in AD. Franz diffusion cell experiments demonstrated 3.29-fold and 4.67-fold increases in the 24-h cumulative permeation of betamethasone dipropionate (BDP) and betamethasone sodium phosphate (BSP), respectively, compared with passive application. In vivo fluorescence imaging showed greater penetration depth of fluorescein sodium following microneedle treatment, while histological examination revealed transient epidermal disruption. In a 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (DNCB)-induced AD mouse model, the combined treatment was associated with reduced epidermal thickening, mast cell accumulation, and serum IgE and IL-13 levels. In a pilot split-body clinical study involving 28 participants with mild-to-moderate AD, the microneedle + compound betamethasone-treated side showed greater improvements in Scoring Atopic Dermatitis (SCORAD) intensity and numeric rating scale (NRS) pruritus scores than the contralateral microneedle + saline control side after 7 days. No serious adverse events were observed during the study period. These findings demonstrate enhanced cutaneous permeation of compound betamethasone following microneedle-assisted application and provide preliminary evidence of therapeutic activity and short-term tolerability in AD.

studies.title: Mast cell-derived SPP1 promotes colorectal cancer liver metastasis by suppressing BTG1-mediated JUN degradation.
studies.journal: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
studies.authors: Wei, Zhao-Yi, Lv, Feng, Hao, Liang, Li, Jian-Wen et al.
studies.abstract: The role of mast cells in colorectal cancer (CRC) liver metastasis remains controversial. This study aimed to explore the effect of mast cells on the CRC liver metastasis and the underlying mechanism. The bulk-seq, scRNA-seq datasets and clinical samples were integrated to identify the association of mast cells and the SPP1-CD44 signaling and BTG1 with CRC liver metastasis. The effect of mast cells on CRC was determined using co-culture systems and xenograft model. The cell viability, migration, invasion, and epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT) were determined. The interaction of BTG1 and JUN was also determined. The integrated analysis of bulk-seq, scRNA-seq datasets revealed that activated mast cells and downregulation BTG1 expression were associated with CRC liver metastasis, and activated mast cells exhibit enhanced SPP1-CD44 signaling with CRC cells. CRC cell supernatants promote mast cells activation and downregulate BTG1 expression and upregulated SPP1 expression. Conversely, activated mast cells promote CRC cell viability, migration, invasion, and EMT activity via SPP1 secretion. Blocking SPP1 suppress the effect of activated mast cells on CRC cells. Mechanistically, BTG1 acts as a tumor suppressor by directly binding to JUN and promoting its degradation. BTG1 knockdown enhances tumorigenicity in vitro and promoted liver metastasis in vivo, these effects partially reversed by JUN inhibition. Mast cells drive CRC cells liver metastasis through modulation of the BTG1-JUN signaling axis. BTG1 acts as a tumor suppressor in CRC by directly binding to JUN and promoting its degradation, thereby restraining oncogenic signaling.

studies.title: Activity-Guided Identification of Prot2633 as a Major Proteolytic Contributor to the Reduced Allergenicity of Lacticaseibacillus paracasei XJ-003-Fermented Milk.
studies.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
studies.authors: Ma, Ruida, Xu, Yunpeng, Guo, Zihao, Zhang, Haiyun et al.
studies.abstract: Lactic acid bacterial fermentation offers a food-compatible strategy for reducing milk allergenicity, but the responsible proteolytic components remain poorly defined. We evaluated milk fermented with Lacticaseibacillus paracasei XJ-003 using pooled sera from milk-allergic donors and characterized its protease system. Activity-guided purification of cell pellet lysates yielded Prot2633, a native protease preparation dominated by S1 serine protease SP2685 and S9 oligopeptidase SP1714. Prot2633 showed maximal activity at pH 6.5 and 43 °C and reduced IgE-binding reactivity of casein and whey within defined hydrolysis windows. In sensitized BALB/c mice, XJ-003-fermented milk and Prot2633-hydrolyzed milk attenuated antibody responses, mast cell degranulation, Th2-associated inflammation, and intestinal barrier disruption, while producing treatment-associated changes in gut microbiota. These findings identify Prot2633 as an important, but not exclusive, proteolytic contributor to the reduced allergenic reactivity of XJ-003-fermented milk and support activity-guided development of protease-assisted dairy processing.

studies.title: Key Players and Pathways of Mast Cell Activation in Urticaria.
studies.authors: Jahn, Carolin, Gialama, Dimitra, Pashuk, Margarita, Xiang, Yi-Kui et al.
studies.abstract: Mast cells (MCs) are the principal effector cells in urticaria, orchestrating the release of mediators that drive wheal formation, angioedema, and pruritus. Although activation of MCs via the immunoglobulin (Ig) E and its high-affinity receptor (FcεRI) axis, including autoimmune urticaria mediated by IgE and IgG autoantibodies, remains the best characterized pathway, increasing evidence indicates that additional mechanisms contribute to disease pathogenesis. These include Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2 (MRGPRX2), c-Kit (key regulator of mast cell differentiation, proliferation, and survival), complement, coagulation, and the microbiome. Emerging data suggest that multiple pathways may coexist and interact within individual patients. Variability in the relative contribution and interaction of these pathways likely underlies the clinical heterogeneity of urticaria and the differences observed in therapeutic responses. Improved characterization of molecular endotypes and identification of reliable biomarkers, will be essential for advancing precision medicine in urticaria, especially as emerging therapies, including BTK, KIT, and JAK inhibitors, provide opportunities to selectively target distinct components of disease pathogenesis. This review provides an overview of key players, signaling pathways and molecular mechanisms involved in MC activation and degranulation in urticaria, focusing on chronic urticaria, especially chronic spontaneous urticaria. People who live with chronic urticaria often experience repeated episodes of itchy wheals and swelling. These symptoms happen when certain immune cells, called mast cells, release substances that irritate the skin. For many years, researchers believed that mast cells were activated mainly through a single pathway involving a molecule called immunoglobulin E (IgE). This pathway is still important, but it does not explain the full range of symptoms or why people respond differently to treatment. Why was the study done? Researchers wanted to understand why chronic urticaria looks and behaves so differently from person to person. They also wanted to learn why some people improve with standard treatments while others do not. To answer these questions, they explored the different ways mast cells can become activated. What did the researchers do and find? The research team reviewed scientific studies that describe how mast cells respond to signals in the body. They found that mast cells can be activated through many pathways, not just IgE. These include receptors such as MRGPRX2 and Kit, as well as signals from the complement system, the blood‑clotting system, and even the microbiome. Several of these pathways may be active at the same time in the same person. What do these results mean? These findings show that chronic urticaria is a complex condition with multiple biological drivers. Understanding which pathways are active in each person may help doctors choose more effective treatments. This knowledge also supports the development of new therapies that target more than one pathway, moving the field closer to truly personalized care.

studies.title: Diet-stress interactions in gut barrier dysfunction and metabolic inflammation.
studies.authors: Tičinović Kurir, Tina, Pavlović, Nikola, Šantić, Roko, Lerotić, Ivana Irma et al.
studies.abstract: The intestinal barrier is a dynamic host-microbe interface that contributes to metabolic homeostasis. Chronic psychological stress and adverse dietary patterns can each disturb microbiota, mucus, junctional, and inflammatory processes. This review evaluates the evidence for convergence of diet- and stress-responsive pathways at the intestinal barrier and their possible relevance to metabolic inflammation. Activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) and sympatho-adrenomedullary axes, together with adverse dietary exposures, converges on the gut microbiota and epithelial barrier. Stress-related corticotropin-releasing hormone/mast-cell signalling, glucocorticoids, and catecholamines can remodel mucus and tight junctions, while high-fat, Western-style, ultra-processed, or prolonged substrate-restricted diets reduce butyrogenic support and may shift bile-acid metabolism toward barrier-disruptive secondary bile acids. The resulting mucus erosion and tight-junction remodelling, including reduced occludin/ZO-1 and increased pore-forming claudin-2, increase permeability and facilitate lipopolysaccharide translocation. LPS-TLR4-NF-κB signalling provides inflammatory priming and can converge with diet- and stress-related danger signals on the NLRP3 inflammasome, promoting IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6 release. These pathways plausibly contribute to obesity, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, although direct human evidence for a true diet × stress barrier interaction remains limited. Preclinical studies provide mechanistic support for overlapping diet- and stress-responsive barrier pathways, and acute human stress studies provide functional permeability evidence. Human dietary evidence is more often indirect, and direct factorial studies of diet × stress effects on barrier function are largely absent. The proposed framework should therefore be treated as a testable synthesis rather than an established causal model.

studies.title: Outcome measures in long COVID clinical trials: a review.
studies.authors: van Rhijn-Brouwer, Femke C C, de Canson, Chloé, VanDerNagel, Joanneke E L, Westerhuis, Xandra et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID is a multisystem disease that affects approximately 10% of people after a SARS-CoV-2 infection. In the absence of curative treatment, high-quality clinical treatment trials are urgently needed for long COVID. There is significant overlap between long COVID and other infection-associated chronic conditions, in particular myalgic encephalomyelitis. As such, trial design for long COVID can benefit from prior experience in this field. In this review we explore outcome measures in long COVID and myalgic encephalomyelitis clinical trials to survey current practices, and provide recommendations for future clinical trials. PubMed and Clinicaltrials.gov were searched for clinical trials on long COVID and myalgic encephalomyelitis that featured a biomedical intervention. 37 myalgic encephalomyelitis and 68 long COVID trials were identified that used 397 outcome measures in total. We then critically assessed the relevance of these outcome measures for patients. Long COVID trial design could be improved by incorporating outcomes that address important symptom clusters such as post-exertional malaise, dysautonomia and mast cell activation. Clinical assessments, physical tests and biomarkers can supplement patient reported outcome measure data, if safety, feasibility and applicability are carefully considered. Lastly, safety of the intervention is rarely adequately evaluated. We recommend a concerted effort to include patient input at all steps of clinical trial design, execution and evaluation.

studies.title: Factors influencing the professional identity of medical care assistants: a qualitative study.
studies.authors: Zhao, Jing, Xu, Dongping, Hong, Ying, Chang, Hongjuan et al.
studies.abstract: This study aimed to explore the factors influencing the professional identity of medical care assistants (MCAs) and to interpret relevant findings through the lens of social identity theory, thereby informing strategies to support professional identity and workforce stability. A qualitative descriptive research design was adopted. Using purposive sampling, 15 MCAs from a tertiary grade A hospital in Wuhan, Hubei province, China, were recruited for one-to-one semistructured interviews. Data were analyzed via inductive thematic analysis, and this report was prepared according to the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ). Four themes and eight subthemes were identified: social evaluation influencing experiences of professional value and dignity, including recognition of professional value and challenges to professional dignity; role positioning and practical needs constructing professional meaning, including professional role positioning and practical needs as a driving factor; care interactions and self-adjustment shaping professional experiences, including communication and trust building and professional competence and emotional adjustment; and team and organizational support strengthening professional identity, including acceptance by the healthcare team and professional training and institutional support. Participants described social evaluation, professional role positioning, recognition or devaluation experienced during care interactions, team acceptance, and organizational support as factors influencing their professional identity. Practical needs primarily shaped occupational choice and intentions to remain, whereas self-adjustment functioned as a coping process within emotionally demanding care experiences. Accounts from participants suggest that the professional identity of MCAs is shaped by social evaluation, role positioning, care interactions, and team and organizational support within the context of their workplace. Healthcare institutions and relevant employers should enhance social and team recognition, clarify responsibilities of the role and collaboration boundaries, improve training and supportive employment arrangements, and consider performance-based incentives to support professional identity and workforce stability of MCAs.

studies.title: Cross-cultural care awareness and self-perceived skillfulness among medical students in Egypt: a national study.
studies.authors: Deibes, Tasneem, Hegazy, Adham, Nofal, Abdallah Adel, Abdelmageed, Ahmed et al.
studies.abstract: Cross-cultural care (CCC) enables effective, patient-centered care for individuals from diverse backgrounds. Despite its importance in improving care quality and reducing health disparities, evidence on CCC among medical students in Egypt remains scarce. This study assessed medical students' cross-cultural self-perceived skillfulness and cultural awareness, examined their association, and identified sociodemographic and educational factors linked to both. A multicentric cross-sectional study was conducted between November 2025 and March 2026 across 14 Egyptian medical schools. Using convenience sampling, 1,645 medical students from all academic years and interns participated. Data were collected using an online questionnaire that included sociodemographic and educational factors, the Modified Cultural Awareness Scale (mCAS), and the Harvard CCC Survey skillfulness subscale. Statistical analyses included correlation, group comparisons, and multivariable linear regression. Among 1,645 participants (mean age 21.8 ± 1.9 years; 53.7% female), the mean self-perceived cross-cultural skillfulness score was 3.55/5 (SD 0.78). Students felt most skilled in identifying a patient's Arabic literacy and taking a social history, and least skilled in counseling on complementary and alternative medicine and identifying patient mistrust. The mean total cultural awareness score was 4.69/7 (SD 0.75), highest in the Cognitive Awareness and Clinical Issues domains and lowest in General Educational and Research Experience. Higher awareness was associated with advanced English fluency and greater perceived adequacy of clinical experience and training (all p < 0.001), and skillfulness correlated positively with total awareness (r = 0.383, p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, advanced English fluency, prior cultural sensitivity training, and all four cultural awareness domains were independently associated with skillfulness (all p ≤ 0.036). Among medical students in Egypt, self-perceived cross-cultural skillfulness was at an intermediate level and was independently associated with advanced English fluency, prior cultural sensitivity training, and greater cultural awareness across all mCAS domains. These findings identify cultural sensitivity training and cultural exposure as actionable targets for strengthening cross-cultural skillfulness in the medical curriculum.

studies.title: MRGPRX2 in Allergic and Immune-Mediated Diseases: Mechanisms, Clinical Relevance, and Therapeutic Translation.
studies.authors: Reinisch, Walter, Li, Yi, Xiong, Pengju, Li, Haijian et al.
studies.abstract: Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2 (MRGPRX2) is a mast-cell-enriched receptor that mediates immunoglobulin E-independent activation by structurally diverse neuropeptides, host-defense peptides, microbial products, and selected cationic drugs. Its biology links tissue stress and neuroimmune signaling to degranulation, vascular responses, pruritus, barrier dysfunction, and inflammatory amplification, but the extent to which individual diseases depend on this pathway remains uncertain. The strongest clinical rationale begins with non-IgE-mediated immediate drug hypersensitivity, for which MRGPRX2 provides a direct mechanistic framework, although rocuronium illustrates the need to distinguish human MRGPRX2 pharmacology from murine Mrgprb2 and from IgE-mediated perioperative allergy. In atopic dermatitis, preclinical and human skin data support a potential amplifier role in type 2 inflammation and itch, but a randomized phase 2b study of EVO756 did not demonstrate efficacy in an unselected population. In chronic urticaria, challenge, biomarker, and genetic studies suggest an MRGPRX2-responsive subgroup within a heterogeneous disease, whereas a randomized phase 2b study of EVO756 in unselected chronic spontaneous urticaria was also negative despite earlier pharmacodynamic activity. Ulcerative colitis provides additional human tissue evidence for an MRGPRX2-associated mast-cell circuit, although murine Mrgprb2 studies show context-dependent protective and pathogenic effects. Emerging evidence in chronic prurigo, allergic contact dermatitis, asthma, mastocytosis, rheumatoid arthritis, synovial inflammation, and neurogenic inflammation is also considered, with explicit separation of human observations from mouse-model evidence. We integrate these findings with receptor pharmacology and early clinical development, emphasizing evidence hierarchy, validated biomarker needs, patient selection, tissue target engagement, safety, and trial design. Current data support MRGPRX2 as an investigational endotype-defining pathway rather than a universal driver of allergic or immune-mediated disease.

studies.title: Age-related biomechanical and structural remodeling of human middle cerebral arteries.
studies.authors: Halvorsen, Samuel C, Mlawer, Samuel J, Then, Reuben M, Stein, Thor D et al.
studies.abstract: Proper cerebral artery function is essential for maintaining the brain's microenvironment. The multilayered organization of cellular and extracellular matrix (ECM) constituents enables large cerebral arteries to accommodate pulse pressure and ensure both effective blood distribution and protection of the microcirculation. However, aging and disease induce compositional and structural remodeling in cerebral arteries, such as the middle cerebral artery (MCA), which can alter biomechanical properties and increase susceptibility to cerebrovascular conditions including atherosclerosis and aneurysms, both major contributors to stroke. Understanding how age-related changes in arterial structure and composition influence biomechanical behavior is critical for improving prediction of cerebrovascular risk. In this study, we characterized the age-dependent elastic and viscoelastic properties of human MCAs and related these changes to ECM structure and composition using imaging and biochemical assays. Our results demonstrate that aging is associated with increased stiffness and stress relaxation in MCAs. Biochemical analyses revealed age-related increases in collagen and glycosaminoglycan (GAG) content, both of which correlated with altered mechanical properties. Histological staining further showed denser collagen organization within the adventitia and elevated GAG presence, consistent with mechanical and biochemical findings. Additionally, multiphoton imaging under mechanical loading provided insight into layer-specific collagen reorganization in the adventitia. Collectively, these findings elucidate key age-dependent alterations in the structure-function relationship of human cerebral arteries and provide a mechanistic basis for increased cerebrovascular risk with aging. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Age-related remodeling of the extracellular matrix is a fundamental driver of tissue dysfunction, yet its effects on human cerebral artery mechanics remain poorly understood. In this study, we combine biomechanical testing, biochemical assays, histology, and multiphoton microscopy to characterize structural and functional remodeling of human middle cerebral arteries across a broad age range. We demonstrate that aging is associated with increased arterial stiffness and viscoelastic relaxation, accompanied by elevated collagen and glycosaminoglycan content. By directly linking extracellular matrix composition and organization to biomechanical function, this work provides new insights into the mechanisms governing cerebrovascular aging. These findings establish an important structure function framework for understanding vascular tissue remodeling and have broader implications for age related vascular dysfunction, mechanobiology, and biomaterials research.

studies.title: Effect of a breathing mask on type 2 mediator responses to subzero exercise in individuals without asthma.
studies.authors: Hanstock, Helen, Ainegren, Mats, Andersson, Erik P, Bäckebjörk, Ella et al.
studies.abstract: Current evidence suggests that heat and moisture-exchanging breathing masks (HME) protect against exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (EIB). We aimed to explore whether mast cell mediator release following exercise in subzero conditions is affected by the use of an HME. To this end, 23 healthy, recreational-competitive endurance athletes aged 18-53 years without asthma performed a 30-min warm-up followed by a 4-min maximal, self-paced running time trial, with and without HME, in -15 °C. Concentrations of leukotriene E LTE₄ decreased after the 4-min maximal exercise test (p < 0.001), with no significant interaction with HME use. There was no effect of exercise alone nor HME on 11β-PGF2α responses to exercise. Taken together, we observed limited evidence of type 2 inflammation in healthy participants after brief, high-intensity exercise in the cold, with and without use of an HME. As the biomarker outcomes reported here were secondary and not powered in advance, these exploratory findings in a healthy cohort warrant further investigation using more robust airway challenges to better understand early airway responses and the potential for preventative strategies in athletes. studies.title: A pectic polysaccharide from Lonicera japonica alleviates DNCB-induced atopic dermatitis-like inflammation associated with gut microbial and metabolic alterations and reduced cutaneous JAK2/STAT3 activation and Th17 responses.
studies.authors: Jin, Mingzhu, Hu, Yue, Ding, Mengmeng, Cheng, Jiayue et al.
studies.abstract: Lonicera japonica Thunb. (Jin Yin Hua) is a traditional medicinal herb widely used in East Asia for inflammatory disorders and is commonly included in herbal prescriptions for atopic dermatitis (AD). WLJP-025p, a homogeneous pectic polysaccharide isolated from Lonicera japonica, has shown anti-inflammatory and anti-AD potential, but its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic effect of WLJP-025p on DNCB-induced AD-like dermatitis in mice and to investigate associated changes in epidermal barrier dysfunction, Th17/IL-17 A-associated inflammation, JAK2/STAT3 signaling, and gut microbial and metabolic profiles. An AD-like mouse model was established in BALB/c mice by repeated application of 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (DNCB). WLJP-025p was orally administered at 30 or 60 mg/kg during the challenge phase, and topical dexamethasone was used as a reference anti-inflammatory control. Disease severity was assessed by skin appearance, dermatitis score, ear thickness, serum biomarkers, and histopathological examination. Skin barrier and inflammation-related proteins were evaluated by immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, Western blotting, and flow cytometry. Colonic injury was examined by hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and Alcian blue-periodic acid-Schiff (AB-PAS) staining. Fecal metagenomic and metabolomic analyses were conducted to characterize gut microbial and metabolic changes. WLJP-025p significantly alleviated DNCB-induced AD-like lesions, as evidenced by reduced erythema, scaling, excoriation, ear swelling, dermatitis scores, epidermal hyperplasia, and mast cell infiltration. WLJP-025p decreased serum IgE, IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-17 A levels. It restored filaggrin (FLG) expression and suppressed thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP) expression in skin lesions, indicating improved epidermal barrier function. WLJP-025p also reduced the proportions of splenic CD3 WLJP-025p exerted protective effects against DNCB-induced AD-like dermatitis. Treatment was accompanied by restoration of epidermal barrier-related markers, reduced JAK2/STAT3 activation and Th17/IL-17 A-associated inflammatory signaling, improved gut barrier integrity, and alterations in gut microbial and fecal metabolite profiles. These findings indicate that oral WLJP-025p treatment is associated with concurrent intestinal and cutaneous changes in this AD-like model.

studies.title: The new revolution in the treatment of chronic urticaria, present and future of an effective and safe approach.
studies.journal: Italian journal of dermatology and venereology
studies.authors: Giménez-Arnau, Ana M, Barei, Francesca, Salman, Andaç
studies.abstract: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) is a heterogeneous mast cell-driven disease associated with a substantial burden on patients' quality of life. Although most patients achieve disease control with guideline-recommended therapies, a relevant proportion remains refractory, highlighting important unmet needs. This narrative review summarizes current, emerging, and investigational treatments for CSU, discussing them with a pathogenesis-driven and endotype-oriented approach. Established therapies, including second-generation H1-antihistamines and omalizumab, are discussed alongside recently approved and upcoming agents such as dupilumab and Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors, particularly remibrutinib. In addition, novel strategies targeting mast cell survival and activation (antireceptor tyrosine kinase therapies), intracellular signaling pathways (Janus Kinase and Tyrosine kinase 2inhibitors), immunoglobulin E-independent activation (Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2 antagonists), and next-generation anti-immunoglobulin E antibodies are reviewed. Beyond symptom control, the concepts of complete disease control, remission, relapse, and disease modification are examined. The evolving therapeutic landscape of CSU is expected to enable a more personalized management, with the potential to achieve sustained remission and, ultimately, disease modification in selected patients.

studies.title: Perioperative Management of Coexisting Mast Cell Activation Syndrome and Malignant Hyperthermia Susceptibility: A Case Report and Novel Approach to Local Analgesia.
studies.authors: Gearing, Peter Francis, Nack, Thomas, Liyanage, Dinuk, Martis, Walston Reginald et al.
studies.abstract: The coexistence of mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS) and malignant hyperthermia (MH) presents a significant perioperative challenge due to combined risks of anaphylaxis and anaesthesia-related hypermetabolic crisis. We describe the successful anaesthetic management of a man in his 60 s with confirmed MCAS and a strong family history of MH who underwent excision of multiple malignant cutaneous lesions. A structured perioperative strategy incorporating immunological optimisation with omalizumab, strict trigger avoidance, dexmedetomidine and remifentanil procedural sedation, prophylactic corticosteroids and a controlled low-dose adrenaline infusion enabled safe completion of surgery without complication. In the absence of tolerated local anaesthetic agents, dilute adrenaline infiltration was used as an adjunct to improve procedural tolerability. This case highlights the importance of multidisciplinary planning and individualised perioperative strategy in patients with high-risk perioperative profiles.

studies.title: High Level of Component C1q Binding Protein (C1QBP) is Associated With Poor Prognosis and Dysfunction of Mast Cells in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
studies.authors: Li, Wei, Huang, Guangnan, Zeng, Lizhong, Dang, Wenhui et al.
studies.abstract: Component C1q binding protein (C1QBP) is known as an important regulator of mitochondrial plasticity and is involved in antitumor immune response in cancers. Nevertheless, its role in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) still remains largely unknown. C1QBP expression in LUAD and adjacent normal samples was compared by Wilcoxon test, and the corresponding receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was used to estimate its diagnostic value. Associations between C1QBP expression levels and different clinical traits were analyzed by chi-square test; K-M curves were applied for analyzing survival differences, and univariate and multivariate Cox analysis were employed to construct the C1QBP-related nomogram model. Furthermore, GSEA and immune analysis were performed to explore the mechanism. Finally, rhC1QBP was applied to cultured mast cells in vivo to investigate its regulatory effect on mast cell dysfunction, and sh-C1QBP was injected into LUAD xenograft mice to explore the effect of C1QBP knockdown on tumor growth in vivo. The C1QBP expression level, with a preferable diagnosis effect, was significantly different between LUAD and normal samples, and was notably interrelated with gender, TNM stage, and Fustat in LUAD patients. LUAD patients with high C1QBP levels displayed lower survival rates. Our nomogram based on C1QBP expression and T stage displayed decent prediction capability. There was a significant difference in C1QBP expression in plasma cells, regulatory T cells (Tregs), activated CD4 memory T cells, resting mast cells, and eosinophils between LUAD patients and the controls. Upregulation of C1QBP with rhC1QBP treatment promoted mast cell ferroptosis through interacting with the Cullin3 protein. While Fer-1, a ferroptosis inhibitor, counteracted rhC1QBP induced ferroptosis in mast cells. Knockdown of C1QBP inhibited tumor growth in xenograft mice. C1QBP may be a promising potential prognostic biomarker in LUAD and a potential therapeutic target by affecting the immune microenvironment of LUAD patients.

studies.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is dystrophin-deficiency skeletal and cardiac muscle disease. Protein post-translational modification (PTM) and aberrant immune cell activation play a key role in its pathogenesis. Our study aims to investigate isonicotinylation (Kinic)-associated signature modulatory patterns in mast cells and DMD pathogenesis. We first performed integrated bioinformatic methods, such as WGCNA, GSVA, and CIBERSORT to identify Kinic and mast cell (KM)-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in DMD patient muscle bulk profiles (GSE38417 and GSE109178). Next, consensus clustering and assembling machine learning pipeline identified KM-associated diagnostic model and molecular subgroups in training the DMD patient muscle bulk set (GSE6011), and then, diagnostic model performance was examined in the independent DMD patient muscle bulk set (GSE32720). In addition, SHAP analysis decoded the main contributor in KM-associated diagnostic model construction, and contributor molecular and immune characters in DMD were estimated in GSE6011 and the DMD mouse muscle single-cell transcriptomic dataset (GSE213925) assisted by computational virtual cells. In addition, the deep learning framework and network pharmacology identified the drug synergy strategy for the treatment of DMD. Finally, the KM-associated molecular patterns can potentially guide the diagnostic and molecular stratification for DMD patients. USP18 can be considered an upregulated and mast cell-distributed hub gene involved in pathogenesis of DMD. In addition, finafloxacin with BRD-K10482608 can be considered two potential therapeutic candidates for DMD patient clinical applications. Our investigation described a novel forecasting and therapeutic model for DMD patients, which potentially enhances DMD patient clinical translation.

studies.title: Beyond Neuroinflammation: Targeting the Microbe-Barrier-Brain Axis Through Precision Nutrition in Neurological Long COVID (Neuro-PASC).
studies.authors: Velázquez De Castro-Bono, Amador, Castro-Luna, Gracia, Guil-Guerrero, José Luis
studies.abstract: Post-acute Neurological Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (Neuro-PASC) contribute substantially to Long COVID-related disability, with cognitive impairment, chronic fatigue, dysautonomia, and neuropsychiatric symptoms among its most debilitating manifestations. Although its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood, evidence implicates persistent immune activation, intestinal barrier dysfunction, microbiota dysbiosis, microbiome-derived metabolic alterations, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroimmune interactions in sustaining neuroinflammation and neurological impairment. This narrative review examines precision nutrition as a potential pathway-oriented strategy for Neuro-PASC. We synthesise evidence linking the gut microbiota, intestinal permeability, immunometabolic pathways, mitochondrial function, and neurological outcomes, while evaluating nutritional interventions targeting these mechanisms. We focus on candidate biomarkers, including serum zonulin, fatty acid-binding protein 2 (FABP2), faecal short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), and the kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratio, which may support patient stratification and personalised nutritional strategies. We also propose a stepwise framework involving dietary stabilisation, functional foods, targeted supplementation, and microbiome-based interventions, alongside practical considerations for post-exertional symptom exacerbation, dysautonomia, and mast cell-related symptoms. Finally, we identify priorities for future research, including multi-omics integration, artificial intelligence, digital health, and biomarker-stratified randomised controlled trials. Because current evidence remains predominantly observational and mechanistic, precision nutrition should be considered a complementary strategy requiring rigorous clinical validation.

studies.title: Somatic Blood Mosaicism and Psychiatric Disease: Current Evidence and Causal Limits.
studies.authors: Belbe, Andrada-Adelaida, Pîrlog, Lorin-Manuel, Pilatec, Alissia-Nicoleta, Militaru, Mariela-Sanda et al.
studies.abstract: Somatic blood mosaicism is an established feature of ageing and a heterogeneous marker of haematologic cancer and inflammatory and vascular risk, but its psychiatric evidence base remains small. This structured critical narrative review evaluates mutation-defined clonal haematopoiesis, clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), autosomal mosaic chromosomal alterations (mCAs), and sex-chromosome loss while separating probable developmental mosaicism from adult-acquired blood clonality. Direct human evidence comprises seven methodologically heterogeneous studies. Psychiatric CHIP findings rely mainly on one prospective UK Biobank cohort of 360,451 participants, in which CHIP was associated with any incident psychiatric disorder (hazard ratio 1.15), particularly major depressive and substance-use disorders. Separate studies report excess mosaic losses in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder and autosomal or X-chromosome mosaicism in suicide. Clone-size gradients and lesion-specific findings add biological structure, but do not provide independent replication. Most mechanistic support comes from cardiovascular, stroke and neurodegenerative research: mutant myeloid cells can alter inflammasome signalling, endothelial function, thrombosis and tissue macrophage behaviour. These pathways make indirect brain effects plausible without establishing a psychiatric mechanism. Blood detection also cannot date a mosaic event or demonstrate the same clone in neural tissue. Taken together, the available evidence supports somatic blood mosaicism as a potentially informative marker of psychiatric heterogeneity and shared inflammatory, vascular and ageing-related biology, but does not establish a causal blood-clone-to-brain pathway. Routine psychiatric screening for CHIP or mCAs is therefore not currently justified. The immediate research priority is independent replication in longitudinal cohorts with repeated sequencing, detailed exposure and treatment histories, and direct testing of inflammatory, vascular and neuroimaging intermediates capable of distinguishing cause, consequence and shared risk.

studies.title: Colonic Mast Cell Density and Diarrhoea: Evidence Against a Threshold Effect in Biopsies From 3508 Patients.
studies.authors: Langreiter, Marlena, Genta, Robert M, Schreiner, Philipp
studies.abstract: Elevated mast cell (MC) counts in colonic biopsies are frequently observed in patients with chronic diarrhoea or unspecific abdominal symptoms, potentially leading to a diagnosis of mast cell activation syndrome. However, the clinical relevance of MC quantification in this setting remains controversial. This study aimed to determine the proportion of patients with elevated MC counts who presented with diarrhoea compared to those with normal counts. As a secondary endpoint, we assessed how often MC quantification was performed and what the underlying clinical indications were. We analysed a large US national pathology database with 3.3 million colonoscopies performed between January 2009 and December 2023. Screening colonoscopies for colon cancer detection were excluded. For patients with multiple colonoscopies, only the first procedure was included. This resulted in a total of 2,059,147 colonoscopies. Colonic mast cells were evaluated in 3508 reports (0.17%). In 1167 cases the report contained either the expressions indicating increased MC, or a MC count > 20 MC/high power field (hpf). Diarrhoea was present in 58.3%, 54.1%, 54.7%, 50.0% and 33.3% of patients with MC count of < 20/hpf, 20-39/hpf, 40-59/hpf, 60-98/hpf and ≥ 99/hpf, respectively. These data do not show a relationship between diarrhoea and elevated MC in the colonic mucosa. Therefore, we suggest that the incorporation of MC quantification into the histologic evaluation of colonoscopic biopsies obtained for common GI indications may not be warranted.

studies.title: Shared mediators, divergent networks: a tissue-response hypothesis for discordant phenotypes in chronic spontaneous urticaria and atopic dermatitis.
studies.authors: Ye, Young-Min, Hide, Michihiro
studies.abstract: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) and atopic dermatitis (AD) are pruritic inflammatory skin diseases that share partly overlapping mast-cell-related pathways, including IgE/FcεRI signaling, type 2 inflammation, neuroimmune signaling, and lipid mediator pathways. Yet they usually produce distinct phenotypes: transient wheals and angioedema in CSU and persistent eczematous lesions with inflammation in AD. Whether disease activity in the two conditions fluctuates concordantly or independently within the same patient has not been directly tested. This Perspective proposes that phenotypic divergence reflects the tissue-response network in which mast cell activation is embedded rather than mediator identity alone. In CSU, autoimmune and autoallergic FcεRI-dependent activation, MRGPRX2-related neuropeptide pathways, coagulation/fibrinolysis-C5a signaling, and platelet-activating factor (PAF)/lipid mediators may preferentially converge on mast cells and basophils poised for rapid degranulation within the dermal vascular/perivascular unit. This network favors histamine bursts, endothelial hyperpermeability, neurovascular itch, and feedback-limited wheal formation. In AD, mast cells are embedded in a barrier-disrupted, alarmin-rich neuroepidermal niche, producing a multicellular inflammatory network involving keratinocyte activation, cytokine and chemokine production, neuronal sensitization, itch-scratch cycling, and tissue remodeling, although degranulation and vascular effects may also occur. Neuropeptides and PAF illustrate how shared mediators may be preferentially routed toward vascular leakage in CSU or neuroepidermal inflammatory amplification in AD. This tissue-addressed mast cell output model is proposed as a testable hypothesis for how overlapping inflammatory mediators may generate feedback-limited vascular whealing in CSU but sustained neuroepidermal inflammation in AD. The model emphasizes that shared pathways are preferentially weighted toward different tissue-level outcomes in CSU and AD.

studies.authors: Grama, Monica, Săsăran, Maria Oana, Stan Muntean, Ana, Coman, Delia et al.
studies.abstract: Interleukin-33 (IL-33) is an epithelial-derived member of the IL-1 cytokine family that functions as an alarmin and signals through the ST2 receptor, upstream of type 2 inflammation. Together with thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP) and IL-25, it constitutes an epithelial alarmin triad that orchestrates barrier-related immune responses. Despite substantial mechanistic data, the specific role of IL-33 as a biomarker and therapeutic target in pediatric food-related allergic disease remains insufficiently defined. This systematic review aims to synthesize current evidence on serum and tissue IL-33 in pediatric IgE-mediated food allergy and eosinophilic gastrointestinal disorders (EGIDs), to delineate its association with disease severity, clinical phenotype and oral immunotherapy (OIT) outcomes, and to critically appraise the IL-33/ST2 axis as a candidate biomarker and therapeutic target within the broader epithelial alarmin network. A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus and the Cochrane Library (2010-2026) identified pediatric clinical studies quantifying IL-33 or IL-33/ST2 in food allergy or EGIDs, alongside murine and Fourteen studies fulfilled the inclusion criteria (four pediatric clinical cohorts, ten direct preclinical murine or IL-33 emerges as a context-dependent yet non-redundant component of the epithelial alarmin circuitry in pediatric food-related allergic disease, as candidate biomarker of epithelial inflammation in pediatric EGIDs. However, current clinical evidence is limited and requires validation in larger prospective cohorts.

studies.title: Cutaneous Mast Cells Contribute to the Analgesic Effect of Manual Therapy on CCD Rats.
studies.authors: Yu, Jiayang, Sun, Pingping, Xie, Dong, Zeng, Xinyu et al.
studies.abstract: Lumbar disc herniation (LDH) commonly induces low back and leg pain. Manual therapy (MT) is effective in relieving such pain clinically, but its mechanism remains unclear. Given that acupoint regions are enriched with mast cells that respond to mechanical stimulation, this study explored whether MT alleviates CCD-evoked neuropathic pain and its association with the modulation of cutaneous mast cells. Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats were randomized into sham, chronic compression of dorsal root ganglion (CCD), MT, and mast cell inhibition (MCI) groups. After CCD modeling, MT was administered at BL57 starting on day 4 for 14 days, while MCI received acupoint cromolyn sodium injection. Paw withdrawal threshold (PWT) was measured. Mast cell activation was assessed using immunofluorescence and toluidine blue staining. Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), substance P (SP), Piezo1, and Piezo2 were determined via immunofluorescence; inflammatory cytokines and neurotransmitters by ELISA; expression of MAPK, Piezo1, and Piezo2 by qRT-PCR. MAPK expressions were also detected by Western blot. CCD reduced PWT from day 3, whereas MT significantly restored PWT from day 11. In skin, CCD increased mast cell activation, CGRP, SP, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, interleukin (IL)-6, IL-1β, 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT), and histamine (HA), all of which were attenuated by both interventions. In DRG, CCD elevated p-ERK, p-JNK, and p-p38 MAPK without altering total MAPK expression, and both interventions suppressed MAPK phosphorylation. Piezo2 was upregulated in CCD and reduced by MT and MCI in both tissues. In skin, Piezo1 remained unchanged, while in DRG, CCD downregulated Piezo1 significantly. MT can relieve CCD-induced mechanical allodynia, an effect associated with inhibited cutaneous mast cell activation, attenuated peripheral neuroinflammation, and reduced MAPK hyperphosphorylation in the DRG.

studies.title: Microbial serotonin signalling axes in irritable bowel syndrome: integrative molecular crosstalk among enterochromaffin cells, gut microbiota, neuroimmune circuits, and precision therapeutic engineering.
studies.authors: Mehra, Ravinder Kumar, Singh, Bhanu Pratap, Siddiqui, Shakir, Aldawsari, Mohammed F et al.
studies.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common, often disabling disorder of gut-brain interaction whose molecular basis remains incompletely defined, leaving diagnosis largely symptom-based and treatment largely non-mechanistic. We argue that the serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine; hereafter 5-HT, the primary term used throughout, with "serotonin" retained in less technical contexts) signalling axis-positioned at the interface of the gut microbiota, enterochromaffin (EC) cells, enteric neurons, and the mucosal immune system-is a central, unifying integrator of IBS pathophysiology, and that reframing IBS around this axis offers a route toward mechanism-based subtyping and therapy. We first synthesise how microbiota-driven tryptophan metabolism, short-chain fatty acid and secondary bile acid signalling, and epigenetic regulation of tryptophan hydroxylase 1 (TPH1) shape EC-cell serotonin output, before examining the neuroimmune consequences of dysregulated serotonin secretion-mast cell activation, macrophage polarisation, neurogenic inflammation-and the microbiota-serotonin-gut-brain connectome linking vagal afferent signalling, blood-brain barrier permeability, and central neurotransmitter networks. We then discuss molecular stratification of IBS subtypes through serotonergic endotyping-incorporating SLC6A4 and TPH1 polymorphisms, single-cell transcriptomics, and spatial metabolomics-and critically evaluate next-generation therapeutic strategies, including engineered probiotic chassis, CRISPR-mediated microbial editing, and AI-guided nanomedicine, distinguishing proof-of-concept findings from clinically validated approaches. We conclude that reconceptualising IBS as a disorder of disrupted microbial serotonergic ecosystems, rather than a purely symptom-defined syndrome, offers a coherent and testable framework for biomarker discovery and precision, mechanism-directed therapy, while highlighting the causal-directionality and clinical-translation gaps that must be closed before this framework can be applied at the bedside.

studies.title: Enhancing Surface Icephobic Performance via Spontaneous Fracture Characteristics of Ice Crystals Regulated by Structural Scale Under Shear Flow Conditions.
studies.authors: Jiang, Jiawei, Shen, Yizhou, Xu, Yangjiangshan, Xiang, Junxian et al.
studies.abstract: Icephobic surfaces are conventionally designed by minimizing ice adhesion; however, whether this strategy remains valid under aerodynamic shear remains poorly understood. Here, we reveal that an external flow field fundamentally alters ice adhesion dynamics by inducing the spontaneous fracture and detachment of ice crystals through aerodynamic shear forces. The ice-substrate contact area is primarily determined by the initial droplet size prior to freezing, thereby governing the interfacial adhesion force. Furthermore, Ice detachment is controlled by a competitive interplay between the initial crystal size and its growth orientation, which together determine whether the aerodynamic loading is sufficient to overcome interfacial adhesion. Contrary to the conventional expectation that superhydrophobicity facilitates ice removal, the microstructural anchoring effect inherent to superhydrophobic surfaces impedes spontaneous ice detachment, resulting in substantially higher ice retention compared with conventional hydrophobic surfaces. By contrast, hydrophobic surfaces with nanoscale features exhibit a greater capacity to suppress runback-ice accumulation under flow than conventional hierarchical superhydrophobic surfaces. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for flow-induced spontaneous ice detachment and redefine an icephobicity design concept from minimizing adhesion toward controlling fracture dynamics.

studies.title: Overlapping Post-COVID Conditions: A Case of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis and Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome Triggered by Sequential Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) Infections.
studies.authors: Mayrink Magalhães, Virgínia R, Ribeiro Oliveira, Laura A, Lourenço, Adelina J, Ribeiro Camargos, Isabela et al.
studies.abstract: The rise in post-infectious syndromes following COVID-19, such as Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) and Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS), has become increasingly common in clinical practice, representing an emerging clinical challenge. This case highlights a possible clinical scenario involving the interaction between sequential viral infections - such as the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) - in triggering overlapping chronic conditions. This report presents the case of a patient who developed ME/CFS and POTS following SARS-CoV-2 infection, with a prior history of EBV mononucleosis, and discusses the diagnostic, therapeutic, and pathophysiological implications. A 48-year-old woman with a history of mononucleosis in childhood developed persistent and disabling symptoms after COVID-19 in January 2022. She presented with extreme fatigue, orthostatic intolerance, paresthesia, cognitive dysfunction, and multisystem symptoms. After extensive investigation, she was diagnosed with ME/CFS (early 2023) and POTS (later that year). Mast Cell Activation Syndrome (MCAS) was considered as a hypothesis during follow-up, but objective testing was not confirmatory. Management included pharmacological therapy (including low-dose naltrexone, duloxetine, and palmitoylethanolamide (PEA)), activity adjustments (pacing), and a multidisciplinary approach, with partial and fluctuating responses. This case illustrates how viral infections such as EBV and SARS-CoV-2 may act as sequential triggers in an individual clinical trajectory compatible with the development of ME/CFS and POTS. The symptomatic overlap, the lack of readily available objective biomarkers in this patient, and the need for a predominantly clinical and functional diagnostic approach in her evaluation highlight the complexity of these conditions. This experience also underscores the importance of continued efforts in research, clinical training, and integrated care models to improve the management of patients presenting with post-COVID conditions (PCC).

studies.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
studies.authors: Kothari, Ruchita, Capuzzi, Daniel H, Kilgore, Collin B, Oh, Hyun Jong et al.
studies.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is an autoimmune connective tissue disease characterized by symmetric fibrosis of the skin and multiple internal organs. The mechanisms that trigger early fibrotic changes remain unclear. Mast cells are known to infiltrate human SSc lesional skin in early disease stages, yet the role of mast cells in initiating fibrosis and pruritus in SSc remains debated, in part due to unclear pathways of mast cell activation. Here, we show that mast cells, via the receptor Mrgprb2, contribute to fibrosis in the bleomycin (BLM)-induced skin fibrosis mouse model. Mast cells accumulate in the skin of BLM-treated wild-type (WT) but not Mrgprb2-knockout

studies.title: TLR4 agonists as emerging adjuvants for sublingual allergen immunotherapy: Preclinical evidence and future perspectives.
studies.journal: Allergology international : official journal of the Japanese Society of Allergology
studies.authors: Oka, Tatsuya, Kobayashi, Hiroyuki
studies.abstract: Sublingual immunotherapy (SLIT) is a safe and convenient treatment for allergic diseases, but it usually requires several years to achieve sufficient clinical benefit. Therefore, effective adjuvants are needed to enhance its efficacy and shorten the time required to achieve a therapeutic response. In this review, we summarize the rationale for using Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) agonists as adjuvants for SLIT and describe our recent preclinical findings with synthetic TLR4 agonist derivatives. We established a mouse model of sublingual administration using a small administration volume and a defined retention period after administration. Several TLR4 agonist derivatives enhanced allergen-specific serum IgG responses when administered with allergen. The adjuvant activity of one derivative was abolished in TLR4-knockout mice, indicating that its activity was dependent on TLR4 signaling. A selected derivative was further evaluated in combination with Japanese cedar pollen (JCP) extract. Co-administration of the derivative with JCP extract increased Cry j 1-specific IgG and IgA levels in serum and IgA levels in nasal lavage fluid. It also enhanced allergen-induced IL-10 production without substantially increasing IFN-γ or IL-4 production. Moreover, IgG from mice treated with the derivative and JCP extract more effectively inhibited allergen-induced mast cell degranulation than IgG from mice treated with JCP extract alone. These findings suggest that synthetic TLR4 agonists may enhance SLIT by promoting functional allergen-specific antibody responses. Further studies are needed to confirm their safety and clinical efficacy in humans.

studies.title: Systemic Mastocytosis With Associated Acute Myeloid Leukemia Identified After Induction Therapy: A Case Report and Literature Review.
studies.authors: Han, Joseph, Ghamsari, Farid, Yan, Jessica, Kim, Phyllis
studies.abstract: Systemic mastocytosis (SM) is a rare clonal mast cell disorder, with the vast majority of cases driven by activating KIT mutations, that can coexist with other myeloid hematologic malignancies. There are multiple subtypes of SM, one of which is SM with an associated hematologic neoplasm (SM-AHN), which is the coexistence of SM and a separate neoplasm, often driven by a shared clonal origin. We report the case of a 48-year-old man who initially presented with profound leukocytosis, anemia, and thrombocytopenia and was subsequently diagnosed with AML. After undergoing induction chemotherapy, the patient was found to have less than 5% blasts but perivascular clusters of CD25-positive and CD117-positive cells on a day-14 bone marrow biopsy that were not previously seen, establishing the diagnosis of SM-AML. The patient is currently undergoing consolidation with consideration of allogeneic stem cell transplantation and potential additional maintenance therapy for SM. SM-AHN is a rare entity that has been reported in the literature; however, given its rarity, it does not have a well-established understanding of the drivers of malignancy, risk stratification, and prognostication, among other aspects that are better understood in more common malignancies. Here, we present a case of SM-AHN to contribute to the current literature and improve understanding of this rare entity.

studies.title: From disease activity scores to precision medicine: biomarkers and composite models for risk stratification in chronic spontaneous urticaria.
studies.authors: Elkhalifa, Shuayb, Abuzakouk, Mohamed
studies.abstract: Chronic spontaneous urticaria is a common, mast cell driven condition that presents with wheals, angioedema, or both, and a substantial proportion of patients remain inadequately controlled despite guideline-directed antihistamine therapy. The 2026 guideline has expanded the advanced-treatment options to include omalizumab, dupilumab and remibrutinib, while ciclosporin remains an alternative later-line immunosuppressive option, yet it is organised around treatment response rather than prognosis, so patients with difficult-to-control disease are often recognised only after months of sequential escalation. This narrative review examines the scoring systems and biomarkers available in urticaria and angioedema and considers whether they can support early risk stratification and help identify patients at increased risk of difficult-to-control disease. The validated instruments in routine use, namely the Urticaria Activity Score, the Urticaria Control Test, the Chronic Urticaria Quality of Life Questionnaire, and their angioedema counterparts, measure current disease activity, control, and quality of life rather than long term outcome. A separate body of work has described biomarkers associated with the autoimmune type IIb endotype and with response to omalizumab, including low total IgE, a high ratio of IgG anti-thyroid peroxidase to total IgE, basopenia, and raised inflammatory markers, although most of this evidence is associative rather than prospectively predictive. The distinction between markers of current burden, markers of prognosis, and markers of treatment response is emphasised. Composite models integrating clinical characteristics, patient-reported outcomes, and biomarkers represent a promising approach toward precision management of CSU, although no validated prognostic tool is currently available for routine clinical use.

studies.title: Endothelial injury and acute-phase inflammatory mediators converge to drive dengue severity.
studies.authors: Anshad, Abdul R, Atchaya, Muthuvel, Saravanan, Shanmugam, Murugesan, Amudhan et al.
studies.abstract: Severe dengue infection is characterized by endothelial injury and systemic inflammatory complications. To better understand the mechanisms underlying disease severity, we investigated a broad panel of circulating inflammatory and endothelial mediators in patients with clinical dengue infection. A prospective cross-sectional study was carried out involving 111 dengue patients and 42 healthy controls. Among the dengue cases, 85 were identified as primary, while 26 were classified as secondary dengue infections. Serum levels of endothelial markers (Ang-2, CXCL10, MCP1, and TRAIL), liver dysfunction and acute-phase markers (CRP, galectin 3, and serum amyloid protein), systemic inflammatory mediators (MIF, TNF-α, IL-1β), mast cell-derived proteases (chymase, tryptase), and tissue repair markers HGF, IL-10, IL-1Ra) were quantified using ELISA and Luminex multiplex assays. Correlations among serum analytes, severity indicators, and haematological markers were also explored. Several biomarkers, Ang-2, CXCL10, TRAIL, CRP, MIF, IL-1Ra, TNF-α, and chymase showed differential expression across severity groups, indicating coordinated endothelial and inflammatory activation. Stratification of patients with primary-secondary dengue also followed a similar pattern except IL-1β, which had significant differential expression across the cohorts. Ang-2 showed strong positive correlations with markers of hepatic dysfunction, including ALT, AST, and bilirubin, suggesting a link between endothelial injury and liver involvement. Severe dengue is driven by the coordinated activation of endothelial dysfunction, acute-phase responses, mast cell mediators, and counter-regulatory pathways. These processes collectively contribute to vascular leakage and organ injury, reinforcing the value of biomarkers such as Ang-2, CXCL10, CRP, and chymase for severity assessment.
